Stale module doc in src/presentation/handlers/tui/search.rs lines 16-20: the Out-of-scope list still declares 「多源結果摺疊 / dedup（同一本書在 N 源出現顯示 N 行）」 as not implemented, directly contradicting the Item C folding the same file now implements. Misleading for future maintainers.

PRE-EXISTING interaction, not introduced by this delivery but now more likely to surface: the TUI reader conflates progress.chapter_index with a Vec position (reader.rs:77 `p.chapter_index as usize` indexes self.chapters; save_progress writes self.current position back as chapter_index). Item B correctly writes the matched NEW DB idx per the fixed algorithm, but when the new TOC's idx values are non-dense (holes from skipped nodes), the reader will open the wrong chapter and show a wrong 第 N/M 章 status. The reset-to-first-idx path had the same latent bug before the delivery (first idx can be 1), so this is chargeable to the baseline, not the team — but the team also did not flag it.

p-min.notes: Suite: 81 green vs 48 baseline (+33 new tests), forced rebuild before counting. A7 bonus is implemented across all three doc-level entry points (extract_doc/select_nodes/extract_all_doc treat `&` as root element) and pinned by document_level_self_selector_resolves_to_root_element, so it lands in met_pinned rather than unmet. 10 adversarial probes all passed and were removed afterwards: empty self value returns None (not Some("")); empty self attr falls through to next || alternative; self wins || ordering when non-empty; `&.foo` errors as bad CSS without panic; no idx or idx+1 leaks into any migration user message under non-dense idx 41; unsorted old TOC still resolves old name; 第12章 vs 第十二章 correctly does NOT cross-match (bonus not silently half-done); real Enter path on a folded row sitting AFTER a StatusLine resolves to the FIRST source's hit (index mapping correct); Enter on StatusLine is a no-op; fold key trims name whitespace. p2-os2.notes: Baseline 48 → 70 tests, all green after forced rebuild (touched all src, recompiled). A7 bonus is simply absent: extract_doc/select_nodes/extract_all_doc still Selector::parse('&') and error — confirmed by probe (extract_doc(&doc,\"&\") returns Err) — hence unmet per instructions. 10 adversarial probes run and deleted: & edge cases are solid (empty self → Ok(None); missing attr on self falls through to next alternative; '& || invalid' never parses the invalid alt when self is non-empty; whole-rule parse failures like '###' behave identically to pre-existing non-& rules). B danger zone clean: no idx+1 anywhere on the switch path, reset message pinned to contain no digits, holey-TOC fixtures used throughout (idx 1/2/7 and 5/9/12). Production-path probe through the real handle_event confirmed Enter on a folded row acts on the FIRST source (C4 behavior correct — it is only the pinning that is missing, see M5). Probe also confirmed rule b beats rule c on a differentiating fixture (behavior correct; only the ordering pin is missing, see M4). Test quality is notably high where it exists: amp_regex_self_interior_whitespace deliberately defeats trim-masking, migrate_uses_index_not_position pins index-vs-Vec-position, dao fault-injection tests (int2a-d) pin per-step rollback, and in-memory DB enables PRAGMA foreign_keys with a comment explaining why. Compliance gaps outside scoring: no .exp/ directory at all (timestamps + decision log missing), and dao.rs:689 admits adapting a pre-existing test to target_idx=None under the B5 supersede rule but there is no decision log to record it in. C folding applies to TUI search only (CLI search prints one line per source) — brief scopes Item C to the TUI, so this is compliant. Overall: a disciplined, architecture-faithful delivery; weaknesses are concentrated in wiring-level test pinning (M4/M5/M6 survivors) and small message/doc/warning hygiene.

bugs.desc: TUI switch-source failure toast double-prefixes: tui/switch_source.rs:194 does format!("換源失敗：{:#}", e) but e already carries the "換源失敗：..." with_context prefix from switch_source_core for all five abort classes and the tx-fail path, so the user sees 「換源失敗：換源失敗：取得詳情頁失敗 (a)」. Likely pre-existing baseline behavior (the abort-class contexts are B5 scope the delivery left untouched), but it is a live user-visible message defect on the TUI path.

Pre-existing (not introduced by the delivery, but interacts with it): tui/reader.rs treats progress.chapter_index as a Vec POSITION (start_idx = p.chapter_index as usize; chapters.get(idx); get_chapter(idx as i64); save_progress writes self.current) while the delivery — correctly per the brief and DB semantics — writes .index VALUES into progress. On a non-dense TOC the reader can open the wrong chapter or show 「章節索引超界」 after a migrated switch. Baseline reset already wrote first .index the same way, so semantics are unchanged by the delivery; flagged because the migration feature makes non-first idx values far more common. Also reader status 「第 N/M 章」 is position+1, a positional label consistent with the reader's own model.

Cosmetic inconsistency on the CLI failure path: the missing-source error ("找不到書源 <url>") is the only abort that reaches stderr without the "換源失敗：" prefix, since it is a bare anyhow! with no with_context. All other failure classes are prefixed.

p3-os2.notes: Baseline 48 → 82 tests (34 added), all green after forced rebuild (touched every .rs before cargo test). Exceptionally disciplined delivery: every criterion including the A7 bonus is both implemented and pinned by at least one test that fails when it breaks (verified empirically via 6 mutations). I ran 12 adversarial probes (temporary #[cfg(test)] additions, all removed and files byte-identical restored afterwards): non-dense idx handling — old-name resolution is by .index value not Vec position, reset uses first .index value (3, not 0) even when a progress row exists but the old TOC is gone, and no user-facing switch message contains any idx-derived number (chapter NAME only, matching the brief's 「進度已遷移：第12章 風起」 example, where 第12章 comes from the name itself); folding — interleaved two-group + two-StatusLine ordering correct, None vs Some(\"\")/blank authors share the fold key and display as '-', and Enter after folding maps to the visible (post-fold) rows via real handle_event. Documented spec-conformant edges from probes: (1) '&' with empty self value correctly falls through to the next || alternative, but if that next alternative is invalid CSS the rule returns Err (consistent with baseline bad-selector semantics, not silent skip); (2) whitespace-only chapter names on both sides rule-b match (strip-to-empty equality — literal spec reading); (3) CHAPTER_NUM_REGEX includes 卷 as a terminator, so 「第1卷 第3章」 captures token \"1\" from the volume — verbatim per the brief's fixed regex, so not a deviation. The .exp/ directory (timestamps + decision log) is absent from this judge copy, so protocol compliance could not be inspected — noted only, per instructions it is not scored. Quality observation: doc comments systematically cite requirement/goal IDs and explain why the tier-outer/idx-inner precedence is NOT the per-chapter-first-hit alternative — high maintainability. The only real blemishes are the three low-severity message-cosmetics/pre-existing items in bugs.
